reader.summary: The defining story of the week was the US-brokered local ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where hundreds of starving residents were evacuated after a rare truce held for several days, with Melania Trump credited as mediator. Simultaneously, Russia's last major independent newspaper, Novaya Gazeta, shut down under sustained Kremlin pressure, with Nobel laureate Murat Bakhitov calling it an "assassination" of press freedom. In Moscow, Putin hosted a large Russia-Africa summit, pitching nuclear power deals, military recruitment, and an anti-colonial partnership to African leaders, while also sealing a 2,000 MW nuclear plant agreement with Ghana. At the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in the United States, European ministers refused to pose for the group photo alongside Russian foreign minister Lavrov, canceling the official photo-op. On the battlefield, a Russian drone strike killed at least 14 people at a Dnipro train station, while Ukraine hit Russian oil refineries before pausing strikes under US pressure. Putin held a rare phone call with the leaders of Finland and Norway, called Elon Musk a "genius" after satellite talks, and both US and Russia vetoed the renewal of the UN Western Sahara peacekeeping mission. Russian espionage and sabotage incidents surfaced in Romania, Germany, and Poland, raising fears of escalation in Europe.

key_events.event: A US-brokered local ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky allowed the evacuation of hundreds of starving residents over several days, with demining and aid operations completed.
Russia's last major independent newspaper, Novaya Gazeta, announced its closure under sustained pressure from Kremlin authorities.
Putin hosted a Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, pitching nuclear deals, military partnerships, and an anti-colonial vision to dozens of African leaders.
European ministers cancelled the G20 group photo in protest over the presence of Russian foreign minister Lavrov at the foreign ministers' meeting in the US.
A Russian drone strike on a Dnipro train station killed at least 14 people, one of the deadliest single attacks on Ukrainian civilian infrastructure in recent weeks.
Leaders of Finland and Norway held a rare direct phone call with Putin to discuss ending the Ukraine war, drawing both praise and criticism from EU partners.
Putin called Elon Musk a "genius" after satellite talks, as Russia accelerates development of a Starlink alternative.
The US and Russia both vetoed the renewal of the UN MINURSO peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, leaving the mission to expire.
Russia extended its ban on most diesel exports through January while planning to ship 2.15 million tons to the US under a new trade arrangement.
Romania, Germany, and Poland reported a series of suspected Russian sabotage and espionage incidents, including a fire near a Romanian weapons factory and arrests in Germany.

emoji_reasons: The Oleshky ceasefire and evacuation (headline 85) was the week's dominant story, representing a rare de-escalation in the Ukraine war.
Novaya Gazeta's forced closure (headline 27) marked a significant blow to Russian independent media and press freedom.
The Russia-Africa summit (headline 50) and the G20 photo-op cancellation (headline 40) underscored the week's intense multilateral diplomacy.

developments.subject: Oleshky ceasefire and evacuation
developments.what_happened: A US-brokered local truce in Russian-occupied Oleshky held for several days, allowing hundreds of starving residents to be evacuated to Ukrainian-controlled territory via Belarus, with demining and aid operations completed.

developments.subject: Novaya Gazeta closure
developments.what_happened: Russia's last major independent newspaper, Novaya Gazeta, announced its shutdown under sustained Kremlin pressure, with Nobel laureate Murat Bakhitov describing the closure as part of the Kremlin's "military campaign."

developments.subject: Russia-Africa summit
developments.what_happened: Putin hosted African leaders in Moscow for a summit focused on nuclear power deals, military recruitment, and positioning Russia as an alternative to Western partners, including a 2,000 MW plant for Ghana and floating nuclear reactors for other states.

developments.subject: G20 tensions over Russia
developments.what_happened: European ministers objected to Lavrov's presence at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in the US, leading to the cancellation of the official group photo and broader diplomatic friction over Russia's role in the forum.

developments.subject: Dnipro train station strike
developments.what_happened: A Russian drone strike on a crowded Dnipro train station killed at least 14 people, with Ukraine warning of further missile attacks on its energy infrastructure.

developments.subject: Nordic leaders call Putin
developments.what_happened: Finland and Norway held a rare direct phone call with Putin to discuss ending the Ukraine war, drawing both support and criticism from other EU partners who felt they were not consulted.

developments.subject: Putin-Musk satellite talks
developments.what_happened: Putin called Elon Musk a "genius" after discussions on satellite technology, as Russia accelerates development of a domestic Starlink alternative.

developments.subject: Western Sahara UN vetoes
developments.what_happened: Competing US and Russian resolutions on Western Sahara were both defeated in the UN Security Council, and the MINURSO peacekeeping mission was not renewed after dual vetoes.

developments.subject: Russia diesel and US trade deal
developments.what_happened: Russia extended its diesel export ban through January while planning to ship 2.15 million tons to the US under a new arrangement, with tankers already en route and New Jersey threatening to block delivery.

developments.subject: Russian espionage in Europe
developments.what_happened: Suspected Russian sabotage and espionage incidents surfaced in Romania, Germany, and Poland, including a fire near a weapons factory, arrests of suspected saboteurs, and a Russian national detained photographing rail infrastructure.

developments.subject: Ukraine strikes on Russian refineries
developments.what_happened: Ukraine hit multiple Russian oil refineries with drone strikes before pausing the offensive under US pressure, with at least one refinery set on fire and the pause seen as a gesture toward Trump-brokered talks.

developments.subject: Ukraine-Russia peace talks outlook
developments.what_happened: Trump said a meeting with Zelenskyy and Putin would be set up soon, Zelenskyy confirmed talks would restart, and the Kremlin said the next round depends on the Middle East situation, while European countries were excluded from the next round.

gone: November peace talks in Abu Dhabi

display.headline: Summit Set After Oleshky, European Sabotage Cluster Escalates
emoji_reasons: The Oleshky ceasefire and the upcoming Zelenskyy-Putin summit are the dominant diplomatic story of the week.
Russian espionage and sabotage incidents across Romania, Germany, and Poland are escalating into a broader European security issue.
The Russian diesel delivery to the US and New Jersey's blocking threat form a concrete ongoing standoff in American ports.
display.tldr: Next week, the US will move from 'talks will be set up soon' to naming a summit venue and delegation, building on the Oleshky ceasefire. European sabotage incidents will escalate into a NATO-level response, and the Russian diesel tanker standoff in US ports will sharpen into legal action.
display.eli5:
Right now, the big news is that a ceasefire held in a Ukrainian city called Oleshky, and hundreds of hungry people got out safely. Trump said a meeting between the leaders will happen soon. Next week, we should hear where that meeting is and who is going. This is the summit logistics story.

In Europe, Russian spies and saboteurs have been caught in three countries this week. Next week, this is set to get worse, with a new incident or a bigger official response from NATO tying the cases together. This is the European sabotage story.

The diesel deal is tricky. Russia is sending fuel to the US, but a state governor wants to block it at the port. This will probably turn into a legal fight over who gets to say no.

A surprise would be something actually happening at a Moscow museum, where the US already warned about a possible big attack. That is unlikely but possible.
